title: Color Contrast and Color Management knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Color Contrast and Color Management”?
questions.explanation: The source curriculum lists “Foreground and background contrast” under “Color Contrast and Color Management”. The lesson applies this syllabus point to a small CSS example and a browser check.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports reliable work with color contrast and color management?
options: Do not rely on color alone; preserve keyboard focus and test text resizing and reflow.
Add !important to every declaration so conflicts disappear.
Assume the newest CSS feature behaves identically in all browsers.
Remove focus styles because a mouse user can see the hovered element.
questions.answer_key: Do not rely on color alone; preserve keyboard focus and test text resizing and reflow.
questions.explanation: The key practice is: Do not rely on color alone; preserve keyboard focus and test text resizing and reflow. For advanced features, inspect the relevant documentation and target-browser compatibility.

questions.prompt: If an example related to “Color Contrast and Color Management” does not look or behave as expected, what is the strongest first response?
options: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
Add several unrelated overrides until the screenshot looks closer.
Only check the default viewport and skip interactive states.
Treat an unused declaration as proof that the browser is broken.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the matched and computed styles, change one cause, and retest the original scenario.
questions.explanation: A repeatable inspection loop is more reliable than layering on overrides: inspect what matched, identify the computed value, change one cause, and retest.
